name: Entacapone
route_note: Oral tablet taken with each levodopa dose, or as a fixed triple combination with levodopa/carbidopa.

discovery.note: A nitrocatechol designed to inhibit peripheral COMT and so extend the effect of levodopa. Year is the priority date of the Orion catechol-derivative patent (US 5,446,194).

tagline: COMT inhibitor that extends each levodopa dose in Parkinson's disease
summary: Entacapone is a reversible, mainly peripheral COMT inhibitor taken with levodopa to reduce end-of-dose 'wearing off' in Parkinson's disease. It was developed by Orion Pharma and is also part of the triple combination Stalevo.
mechanism: When decarboxylation is blocked by carbidopa, COMT becomes the main peripheral route of levodopa breakdown, forming 3-O-methyldopa. Entacapone inhibits this enzyme in the gut and blood, prolonging the plasma half-life of levodopa and increasing the amount reaching the brain.
The result is more sustained dopamine levels and longer 'on' time between doses; because more levodopa is available, dyskinesia can increase and levodopa doses are often reduced.
uses: Adjunct to levodopa/DDC inhibitor in Parkinson's disease with end-of-dose motor fluctuations

history.title: Tolcapone
history.detail: The first COMT inhibitor, tolcapone, is launched; it is later restricted because of fatal hepatotoxicity.

history.title: European approval
history.detail: Entacapone (Comtess/Comtan) is authorised in the EU.

history.title: US approval
history.detail: The FDA approves Comtan, marketed by Novartis under licence from Orion.

history.title: Stalevo
history.detail: The levodopa/carbidopa/entacapone combination Stalevo is approved in the EU and US.

history.title: Opicapone
history.detail: The longer-acting COMT inhibitor opicapone is approved in the EU, offering once-daily dosing.

serious: Neuroleptic malignant-like syndrome on abrupt withdrawal

facts: Unlike tolcapone, entacapone has not been associated with significant liver toxicity and does not require liver monitoring.
